Recruiting guide
Run the meeting.
7 Habits
7 habits of highly
effective recruiting.
01Be proactive
02Begin with the end in mind Have goals in mind.
03Put first things first
04Think win/win
05Seek first to understand, then to be understood
06Synergize 1 + 1 = 3.
07Sharpen the saw Measure twice, cut once.
Step 02 · Get to know them
Seek first to understand,
then to be understood.
Gather information about them so you know how to direct the process. Just like sales, ask questions to find potential objections so you can overcome them before they come up.
Questions to ask
What are your goals for the next 3–5 years?
What are your financial goals?
How are you going to reach your goals?
Ask about job or school. Dig deeper into their intentions with it.
Ask about hobbies and skills.
Ask about relationships.
Find out the hardest things they’ve ever done.
Step 03 · Meeting summary
Tell them where
the meeting is going.
Give a brief outline of what you’re going to talk about in the meeting.
“First I just want to give you a little background on the company, explain the product and compensation, and then tell you about my experience with Vivint and why it’s been so great for me. Then I’ll answer any questions you have.”
Step 04 · About Vivint
Tell them about
the company.
This builds credibility so they know it’s a stable employer. It also shows Vivint is one of the fastest-growing tech companies in the world.
Corporate background
How it started: in a horse trailer, with a $5,000 loan from Todd’s mom.
Goldman Sachs: sold in 2008 for $400M.
Blackstone Group: sold in 2012 for $2.3B.
Now worth $6–10B.
Bring in the key awards Vivint has received.
Ask, “Why do you think I bring this up to you?”
Tell them what it means for us: there’s a huge upside to being with a company still growing this fast at this scale. That growth means real opportunity to hold leadership positions and have influence early.
If they show leadership
“We’re growing faster than we have experienced people to lead, so we have to turn people away. We can’t just take the run-of-the-mill guys. We need the ones who’ll help us build and grow, the best of the best. Right now there’s an opportunity for sharp people to take the reins and ride our success, if they bring the right attitude and work ethic.”
Step 05 · Product
Show them
the product.
Let them see how cool it is and how doable it is to sell. This is your chance to use your sales skills to sell them on the product.
Do a one-sided role-play presentation to cover product and service: features and benefits.
Drop price just like you would on the doors. Give them a price drop-down.
The more amped they are on the product, the more confident they’ll be that they’ll enjoy selling it, and the clearer the picture of what selling it involves.
“Now, understanding what we offer, and knowing we can do it at such a low price, do you think if you worked a full 7 hours you could find at least someone who’d be willing to buy it?”
Step 06 · Explaining pay
Explain
the pay.
Before explaining pay, ask these questions.
“If you did this this summer, would you do it more for the money, the experience, or both?”
Follow up with “Why do you say that?”
“If you knew you’d make (x amount) this summer, would you be willing to give up (their objection)?”
“What’s the highest-paying job you’ve ever worked? How much did it pay? So your employer is saying you’re worth that to them. What do you think you’re worth?”
Show them the Hourly Comparison.
“With most things you really apply yourself to, would you put yourself in the top third, bottom third, or average compared to your peers?”
Show them the Rookie Scenarios.
“In this job, you earn exactly what you’re worth.”
“There’s no other job where, in such a short time, you can prove exactly what you’re worth.”
“Do you feel like if you committed yourself to this you could be successful at it?”
Step 07 · Difficulty
Explain the difficulty
of the job.
Explaining the difficulty adds credibility. Nothing in life that’s really worth committing to is easy.
“In this opportunity, we’re able to earn a substantial income in a short amount of time. The trade-off is a monumental effort. If you want a professional income, you need to put in a professional effort.”
“This will be one of the most difficult things you’ve ever done. It will stretch you, and if you let it, it will make you stronger and more talented. You’ll go on to achieve greater things than you ever expected.”
Give them the benefits of working this hard so they’re motivated to get after it. Light the fire.
Step 08 · Your story
Tell them
your story.
Give them something to relate to.
Why you personally joined
Your experience on the job
What you’ve learned
What’s helped you succeed
The relationships you’ve made
Step 09 · Matt’s Big 3
Matt’s
Big 3.
Explain why each of these 3 simple rules will guarantee them success if they really apply them.
01Work all the hours
02Stay positive
03Don’t give up
Step 10 · Pullback
Recruiting for
the preseason trip.
When recruiting them to come on a preseason trip, make it a two-way decision.
“It not only gives you the chance to decide if this is a good fit, it also gives us the chance to decide if you’re a good fit for the team.”
“…it also gives us the chance to see who proves they’re a good fit for the team, based on how seriously they take the program.”
